tip: The '-s' ending can mean each other: 'setts' means seen one another, from 'se'.
'Sedan' can mean both since and then: 'sedan igår' (since yesterday), 'sedan gick vi' (then we left).
Swedish glues 'the' onto the noun as a suffix '-et': 'huset' = the house, so there is normally no separate word for 'the'.
'Bästa' comes irregularly from 'bra' (good), like English good/best: 'den bästa filmen' = the best film.
'En'-words ending in '-a' form plurals in '-or': 'blomma' becomes 'blommor'.
Verbs whose present ends in '-ar' keep the '-a' in the command form: 'våga' = dare.
'Slappna av' = relax. The little word 'av' is stressed and stays right after the verb.
Verbs whose present ends in '-er' drop the infinitive '-a' in the command: 'försöka' becomes 'försök' = try.
Add '-t' to an adjective to turn it into an adverb: 'hög' becomes 'högt' = aloud in 'läs högt'.
The command form of 'vara' (to be) is 'var', not 'är': 'var modig' = be brave.
Swedish normally has no separate word for 'the'; an 'en'-word adds '-en': 'stol' becomes 'stolen' = the chair.
An 'en'-word already ending in '-a' adds only '-n' for the: 'lampa' becomes 'lampan' = the lamp.
Starting with 'dessutom' (moreover) pushes the verb before the subject: 'dessutom regnar det' has 'regnar' before 'det'.
An 'ett'-word adds '-t' for the: 'garage' becomes 'garaget' = the garage.
'Bli' (become) plus a form like 'stulen' (stolen) makes a passive: 'har blivit stulen' = has been stolen.
'Var snäll och' plus a command form is a polite way to make a request: 'var snäll och hjälp mig'.
In a main clause an adverb like 'fullständigt' normally sits between the two verbs: 'har fullständigt missat' = have completely missed.
Starting with the object for emphasis pushes the subject after the verb: 'det här problemet måste vi lösa' has 'vi' after 'måste'.
When a clause with 'medan' (while) comes first, the main clause begins with its verb: 'lagade hon mat'.
After 'varför' (why) in a reported question the subject stays before the verb: 'varför du är', not 'varför är du'.
Swedish often uses the present tense for future actions: 'ringer' and 'kommer' here mean will call and will arrive.
The suffix '-bar' works like English -able: 'hörbar' = audible, from 'höra' (to hear) plus '-bar'.
'Eftersom' means because and opens a reason clause: 'eftersom det var sent' = because it was late.
'Som' is the all-purpose linking word for who, which or that: 'restaurangen som ligger' = the restaurant that is located.
'Om' means whether in a reported yes/no question: 'frågar om hon vill' = ask whether she wants to.
When 'som' is the object of its clause you may drop it: 'filmen (som) vi såg' = the film we saw.
To feel well uses the verb 'må', not 'känna': 'han mår bra' = he is doing well.
'Hoppas' ends in '-s' so it looks passive, but it is active: 'vi hoppas att' = we hope that.
'Berätta' (tell) needs 'för' before the listener: 'berättade för honom' = told him.
'Ha rätt', literally to have right, means to be right: 'hon har rätt' = she is right.
